prompt:
THE FIRST AWAKENING — HOLLOW HEART
20 SECONDS — 16:9 CINEMATIC WIDESCREEN

8K IMAX. Photorealistic live-action — no 3D-render look, no game-engine look, no game-cutscene aesthetic, no visible CGI aesthetic. Premium invisible VFX are allowed, but everything must appear physically photographed on a real enormous practical location with real human skin, real cloth, real mud, real bark, real atmospheric depth and physically believable lighting.

NO MUSIC. DIEGETIC SOUND ONLY.

REFERENCE CONTINUITY — ABSOLUTE LOCK:
Use the supplied HERO FACE reference for the exact identity of the protagonist: same tan / olive-tan complexion, pale silver-gray human eyes, messy medium-length black/dark-brown hair, exhausted under-eye bags, brutal healed scar crossing the eye and cheek, smaller facial cuts, subtle facial asymmetry, restrained stubble, stressed vulnerable appearance.

Use the supplied HERO FULL-BODY FRONT/BACK reference for his exact body, clothing and Hollow Heart design. Maintain the enormous open chest cavity completely through his torso from front to back. It must NEVER close, heal, disappear, shrink or become a painted wound. Preserve the same lean natural proportions, torn exposed shoulder, filthy dark brown/charcoal clothing, scarred dirty arms, hand wraps, ragged pants and boots.

Use the supplied TRAUMA TREE full-environment and face references as strict visual continuity anchors. Preserve the colossal tilted tree, its sorrowful partially lowered eyes, black viscous tears, enormous mouth-opening beneath the face, sparse upper teeth, ancient carved bark, contorted roots, embedded eyes and faces, petrified figures within the side roots, asymmetrical branches, one enormous spiral branch carrying fractured abandoned houses, and the opposing irregular branch with embedded eyes.

The tree is a GATEWAY THROUGH this region — the mouth opening is not a tunnel extending deep inside a tree. It is a passage through the colossal trunk to another region beyond it. Inside the opening is darkness, dim red atmospheric light and drifting crimson volumetric fog suggesting another space on the opposite side.

ENVIRONMENT:
Nightmarish open basin of wet black-brown soil, shallow muddy puddles, scattered roots and decaying organic debris. Jagged black mountains form distant silhouettes. Sky is extremely dark desaturated blue-charcoal rather than vivid blue, with a deep blood-red horizon behind the mountains. Thin ground fog moves naturally through the basin.

The gigantic tree dominates the landscape and should feel impossibly old rather than fantastical-clean. Bark contains charcoal black, ash gray, faded brown, dirty olive, old moss, subtle dried burgundy staining and occasional muted fungal colors. Tiny mushrooms, patches of sickly moss and extremely restrained strange foliage appear in isolated places.

Broken houses attached to the spiral branch have NO LIGHTS ON. They are abandoned, crooked, partially collapsed and physically built from rotten timber. NO ladders prominently visible.

TREE MOVEMENT MUST BE SUBTLE:
The tree is not cartoonishly animated. Its immense weight must always be felt. The upper trunk may flex only several centimeters as though under ancient internal pressure. Tiny secondary branches respond to wind. The spiral branch can shift almost imperceptibly from its own enormous weight. Loose timber on abandoned houses quietly creaks. Black tears slowly travel down the tree's face. The gateway fog breathes outward in irregular waves. Nothing waves around like tentacles.

MASTERFUL HUMAN PERFORMANCE:
The hero has just realized something impossible has happened to him. His reaction must feel psychologically believable — disbelief first, then physical panic, then awe and terror. No exaggerated screaming, no theatrical horror acting. His breathing becomes shallow. His hands tremble. His pupils search desperately. His posture loses stability. He appears genuinely traumatized and unable to understand what he is seeing.

0:00–0:02.5 — GROUND-LEVEL DISCOVERY
CAMERA almost touching the wet dirt, 20–24mm wide cinema lens, extremely shallow foreground focus.

Begin inches above wet mud and tangled black roots. Tiny puddles reflect distant blood-red sky. The camera rapidly but smoothly pushes forward at ankle level toward the hero as he rises unsteadily into frame.

His battered boots drag through mud. One hand briefly braces against the ground. Dirty fingertips compress wet soil.

Camera tilts upward enough to reveal the enormous open cavity through his torso for the FIRST TIME.

Through the hole we can literally see the environment behind him.

A violent inhalation.

No dialogue.

SOUND:
wet hand against mud,
cloth scraping,
short desperate inhale,
low distant wind.

0:02.5–0:05.5 — THE HOLLOW HEART
CUT HARD to intimate 50–65mm chest-level photography.

The hero looks down.

For approximately half a second he simply cannot process it.

Then his breathing accelerates.

His trembling bare hand slowly reaches toward the edge of the chest opening. Fingers hover, then very cautiously touch ONLY the outer darkened tissue rim.

Physical contact causes his entire body to recoil.

He pulls the hand away sharply, staring at his fingertips in disbelief.

The cavity stays anatomically locked and hyper-realistic:
dark bruised burgundy,
dirty brown-red tissue,
deep almost-black internal folds,
selective damp highlights,
grime where tissue meets shredded fabric.

NO excessive bright pink tissue.
NO gore splashing.
NO transformation.

The emotional horror comes from the impossible absence of his chest.

SOUND:
trembling breath,
faint fabric movement,
a tiny organic contact sound,
heartbeat-like SUB-BASS resonance from the world — environmental, not musical.

0:05.5–0:08.0 — FACE / HUMAN PANIC
SMASH CUT to an extremely high-fidelity 85mm close-up of the exact hero face.

Maximum detail:
individual wet hair strands,
pores,
sweat,
dirt embedded in skin,
scar tissue,
tiny facial scratches,
bloodshot veins around silver-gray eyes,
dark under-eye fatigue.

His eyes move downward toward his chest, then quickly scan his surroundings.

His lower lip barely trembles.

He takes one involuntary backward step.

Do NOT make him scream.

His expression should communicate:
“What happened to me?”
followed immediately by
“Where am I?”

Camera makes an extremely subtle handheld drift, like an operator instinctively reacting with him.

0:08.0–0:12.5 — THE REVEAL
As his gaze rises, MATCH CUT into an extraordinary LOW REAR THREE-QUARTER shot approximately 20 centimeters above the ground behind the hero.

18–21mm cinema lens.

The hero occupies the lower central foreground as a small vulnerable silhouette.

His open chest cavity is partially readable from the angle.

Camera performs a controlled crane/tilt upward while remaining close enough to the ground to exaggerate scale.

The COLOSSAL TRAUMA TREE is finally revealed.

It must dwarf the hero beyond comprehension.

The trunk leans sideways AND slightly forward toward him as though sorrow itself has weight.

The gigantic sorrowful face hangs over the gateway.

One enormous spiral branch fills a major portion of one side of frame, carrying fractured abandoned houses along its curve.

The opposite branch is completely asymmetrical, extending differently and containing several subtle organic eyes embedded within ancient bark.

Massive roots radiate laterally through the landscape.

The composition should make the audience instantly understand:
the human is tiny,
the tree is ancient,
and the only way forward is THROUGH it.

SOUND expands dramatically:
deep wind,
far-off mountain rumble,
wood under enormous tension,
quiet house timbers creaking,
hero breathing.

Still NO music.

0:12.5–0:15.5 — THE TREE SEES HIM
CUT to an extreme telephoto/macro close-up of ONE of the tree's enormous sorrowful eyes.

Not a monster attack.

The eyelid is heavy, half-lowered and exhausted.

The eye must look shockingly organic:
wet cornea,
extremely subtle blood-red vascular detail,
dark iris,
physically realistic reflections,
ancient bark merging naturally into the eyelid.

Thick BLACK VISCOUS TEARS slowly spill downward through deep bark grooves.

The eye makes a tiny movement.

It looks directly toward the hero.

Then the enormous upper lid lowers perhaps 10–15% — almost an exhausted acknowledgment rather than a blink.

The bark around it produces the slightest settling movement.

A distant, extremely low TREE GROAN rolls through the environment — less like a creature growling and more like an ancient building or enormous ship flexing.

0:15.5–0:20.0 — ICONIC FINAL IMAGE
CUT back to an ultra-low, ground-skimming frontal-wide perspective from slightly behind and to the side of the hero.

Camera slowly dollies toward him while simultaneously tilting higher, creating a massive forced-perspective composition:

mud and wet roots enormous in extreme foreground,
hero small in mid-ground,
colossal leaning Trauma Tree towering across the entire background.

The red gateway illumination increases VERY SLIGHTLY.

Dark crimson volumetric fog slowly pours outward from the mouth-opening and spreads close to the ground.

Do not make the light flash or pulse like magic.

The hero takes one slow involuntary step backward.

His shoulders rise with frightened breathing.

He looks upward toward the tree's enormous eyes.

The tree's gigantic spiral branch makes an almost imperceptible weight-driven settling movement.

A few pieces of rotten timber shift on one abandoned house.

Black tears continue traveling down the face.

For the FINAL SECOND, the camera reaches the visual composition we could use as a poster/thumbnail:
the tiny Hollow Heart hero,
his impossible open torso,
the gigantic sorrowful leaning tree,
the red passage,
the spiral of broken homes,
the oppressive dark sky,
the blood-red horizon.

Hold this composition long enough for it to register.

END ON THE HERO'S BREATH AND THE TREE'S LOW DISTANT CREAK.

DO NOT FADE TO BLACK INSIDE THE GENERATION.

CAMERA / EDITING RULES:
Every cut must reveal NEW INFORMATION.
Do not repeat the same composition.
No random montage.
No speed-ramping.
No excessive shaky camera.
No unnecessary orbiting.
No drone-like floating camera.
Camera movement must feel physically operated by an elite live-action cinematography crew.

Use lens language intelligently:
macro/85mm for emotion and material detail,
50–65mm for physical chest interaction,
18–24mm low-angle wides for impossible scale.

Lighting must remain physically coherent between cuts.

REALISM LOCK:
No rubber-looking tissue.
No waxy skin.
No plastic bark.
No painted concept-art appearance.
No oversharpened AI textures.
No duplicated houses.
No duplicated eyes.
No repeated embedded faces.
No morphing anatomy.
No extra limbs or fingers.
No chest-hole deformation between shots.
No facial identity drift.
No costume changes.
No hairstyle changes.
No glowing hero eyes.
No glowing tree eyes.
No cartoon tree motion.
No obvious CGI particles.
No artificial fantasy sparkle.
No videogame VFX.

The impossible imagery must be photographed with absolute physical realism.

OVERALL FEEL:
Not a fantasy game introduction.
Not a horror trailer montage.

This should feel like the opening 20 seconds of an extremely serious, surreal live-action dark-fantasy film — intimate human terror colliding with an impossible world.

The hero's vulnerability is the emotional anchor.
The chest hole is the immediate mystery.
The tree is the first unforgettable statement about this world.

By the end of 20 seconds, the audience should have only one reaction:

WHAT IS THIS PLACE — AND WHAT HAPPENED TO HIM?

Create a hyper-realistic studio portrait of an unforgettable male protagonist with a tan / olive-tan skin tone, designed to feel like a specific iconic lead, not a generic handsome fantasy model.
Core look:
adult male, around late 20s to late 30s
tan / olive-tan skin
medium-long dark hair, never short and never extra long, roughly ear-length to neck-length, with natural volume and texture
hair should have a few loose strands falling across the forehead and/or one side of the face
silver / steel / pale gray human eyes, not glowing, not supernatural
very minimal facial hair only: light stubble or faint scruff, never a heavy beard
strong masculine presence, haunted, intense, memorable, cinematic
Very important identity rule:
Make him feel like a real protagonist with a unique face, not just “a cool rugged guy.”
The underlying face must vary from image to image while staying attractive, believable, and memorable.
Randomize / vary these traits each time:
slightly different face shape
subtle facial asymmetry
different nose shapes: slightly crooked, broken, straighter, longer, wider, sharper, or more Roman
different brow shapes and brow asymmetry
different mouth shapes and lip structure
different jawlines and cheekbones
one eye slightly more hooded, heavier, or smaller than the other
mild under-eye wear, realistic skin texture, pores, faint blemishes, natural irregularities
slightly different hair styling each time while staying medium-long and dark
Scar rule:
Give him one memorable, realistic healed scar or scar pattern, but randomize the scar placement and shape each generation.
The scar should feel brutal, believable, old, and integrated into the face, not decorative.
Possible placement can vary between:
through eyebrow toward temple
across cheekbone
across the nose bridge
from cheek toward mouth line
short vertical forehead scar
broken scar near the eye
irregular scar near jawline
Keep it realistic, healed, and anatomically believable.
Mood / expression:
intense, brooding, soulful, slightly dangerous
calm but powerful
not smiling
emotionally complex, like a lead character with history
should feel memorable even without costume or environment
Framing / presentation:
tight head-and-shoulders portrait
plain neutral gray studio background
soft cinematic lighting
face-first composition
sharp detail on skin, hair, eyes, and scar
highly photoreal
rugged, dramatic, and premium-looking
Important “avoid” rules:
do not make him generic
do not make him look like a fashion model
do not give him short hair
do not give him extra-long hair
do not give him a thick beard
do not make the eyes glow
do not over-design the scar
do not over-stylize the background
do not make him too polished or too pretty
do not make all outputs look like the same exact man unless naturally emerging from the design
Overall goal:
Generate a distinctive, unforgettable, photoreal protagonist portrait with tan skin, medium-long dark hair, pale silver-gray eyes, minimal stubble, slight facial asymmetry, and a realistic memorable scar, while randomizing the underlying identity each time so every result feels like a different strong contender for the same hero concept.

Weapon optional: a long, refined greatsword with a severe silhouette, black metal blade, subtle negative-space openings, and minimal but memorable ritual detail near the guard. The creature must feel like a haunted saint, a watcher, a relic of erased memory, and a recurring world guardian.

prompt:
HYPER-REAL LIVE-ACTION DARK FANTASY IMAGE PROMPT — ANGER REALM — OLDER HERO BEING PULLED BACK BY SHADOW HANDS

Create a single cinematic still frame designed specifically to become the PRIMARY IMAGE REFERENCE for a later video-generation shot.

SCENE PURPOSE:
The older hero is almost at the top of the Anger Realm. He is exhausted, weathered, corrupted, and physically struggling, but he is still forcing himself forward. The realm itself is trying to hold him back. Multiple thin black arms rise FROM THE GROUND BEHIND HIM and grab his shoulders, upper arms, and back, pulling him backward while he leans forward and continues resisting.

This image must clearly establish the correct spatial geography so that a later video model can animate it without confusing where the arms originate.

OLDER HERO HARD LOCK:
Use the exact OLDER hero design.
Longer hair.
Weathered older face.
Visible dark spiral / corruption markings around part of the face.
Battle-worn, dirty, exhausted appearance.
Subtle cuts and dried blood are acceptable but do not make the image gore-focused.
Same established clothing.
Same established longer sword.
Exactly ONE sword.
The sword is held firmly in ONE hand only, low beside him as he struggles forward.
His other arm remains free to balance himself or resist one of the hands.
No extra weapons.
No glowing eyes.

HOLLOW CHEST HARD LOCK — CRITICAL:
The hero has the established TRUE HOLLOW through his chest.

FRONT OPENING → REAL EMPTY AIR/SPACE → REAR OPENING.

It is a genuine opening completely through the torso.

The environment must be visible through the cavity.
The rear opening must remain physically open.
Do not fill it with darkness.
Do not place organs or flesh inside.
Do not seal the back.
Do not cover the rear opening with intact clothing.
Do not place the Hollow in the stomach.
Do not allow any hands or arms to emerge from the Hollow.

COMPOSITION — VERY IMPORTANT:
Use a dynamic REAR 3/4 / SIDE-REAR 3/4 camera angle.

The hero is in the foreground / center-right of frame, moving uphill toward the upper-right or deeper area of the composition.

We should see enough of his back and side to understand:
1. he is moving FORWARD uphill
2. the arms are physically BEHIND him
3. the arms originate FROM THE GROUND
4. they stretch forward from their ground origins and grab him from behind

The camera should be low enough to make him heroic and strained, but high enough that several separate ground cracks behind him are clearly visible.

SHADOW-HAND GEOGRAPHY — ABSOLUTE HARD LOCK:
Every black arm MUST originate from the physical cracked earth.

The image must visibly show:

CRACKED GROUND → FULL BLACK ARM / FOREARM → HAND → HERO

Multiple separate black arms rise from multiple separate cracks in the terrain several feet BEHIND him.

Show the BASE of the arms clearly connected to the ground.

Each arm should have obvious physical length between:
the ground crack where it originates
and
the hand gripping the hero.

The hands do NOT grow from:
his chest
his Hollow
his shoulders
his back
his clothes
his skin
or anywhere on his body.

They are entirely external manifestations coming from the earth.

The majority of the hands grab:
the BACK of his shoulders
upper arms
upper back
edges of clothing near the shoulder blades
sides of his torso

They are pulling BACKWARD.

Do not make ankle-grabbing the main action.
Do not put a wall of hands in front of him.
Do not surround him evenly from every direction.

The visual idea must be unmistakable:

THE HERO MOVES FORWARD.
THE HANDS COME FROM BEHIND.
THE HANDS ARE TRYING TO PULL HIM BACK.

POSE / BODY LANGUAGE:
Capture the hero in the MIDDLE OF THE STRUGGLE, not before it begins.

His torso is leaning strongly forward.
One leg is planted ahead of the other.
His shoulders are being pulled backward while the rest of his body fights forward.
His muscles and posture show strain.
His sword remains in one hand, angled low and slightly backward or beside his leg.
His free arm may be tense near his chest or pulling against one hand gripping his shoulder.

He should look exhausted but absolutely determined.

His expression should communicate:
pain
effort
fatigue
anger
resolve
refusal to surrender

No screaming.
No exaggerated superhero pose.
No passive standing.

ENVIRONMENT — ANGER REALM:
Massive dark fractured terrain climbing toward a distant summit.
Burnt orange, rust-red, charcoal-black atmospheric palette.
Ash and embers blowing aggressively through the air.
Heavy storm wind visibly whipping his longer hair and clothing.
Huge volumetric storm clouds rotating dramatically overhead.
Lightning illuminating portions of the landscape.
Warped ruins and fractured terrain visible in the distance.
Floating debris and ash create strong foreground and background parallax.
No generic bright lava world.
The environment should feel psychological, hostile, and apocalyptic.

LIGHTING:
Cinematic storm lighting.
Warm ember light from below and behind.
Cold lightning accents from the sky.
Strong rim light outlining the hero and the stretched black arms.
Atmospheric volumetric depth.
High contrast but retain detail in the dark arms so their geography is readable.

CAMERA / CINEMATOGRAPHY:
35mm–50mm cinematic lens feel.
Rear 3/4 perspective.
Slightly low camera.
Strong depth of field.
Foreground ash partially crossing the lens.
Clear separation between hero, arms, and stormy background.
Premium live-action realism.
No videogame render look.
No static concept-art pose.

MOST IMPORTANT VISUAL REQUIREMENT:
The viewer must immediately understand that the arms are rooted in the ground BEHIND him and are physically stretched forward to pull him backward while he continues fighting uphill.

NO arms growing from the hero.
NO arms emerging from the Hollow.
NO fused limbs.
NO body transformation.
NO extra sword.
NO glowing eyes.
NO sealed Hollow.
NO incorrect Hollow placement.
NO hands covering the entire chest opening.
NO front-facing wall of hands.

FINAL FEEL:
A tragic, epic, symbolic image of perseverance:
everything behind him is physically trying to drag him back,
but he is still forcing himself forward.

8-SECOND VIDEO — FINAL REVISED MASTER PROMPT
HYPER-REAL LIVE-ACTION DARK FANTASY — ANGER REALM — OLDER HERO PERSEVERANCE

SCENE PURPOSE:
This is the older hero’s final physical and psychological push through the Anger Realm. The realm itself is trying to drag him backward, but he refuses to surrender and keeps forcing himself uphill toward the final destination.

OLDER HERO HARD LOCK:
Use the exact older hero reference.
Longer hair.
Weathered older face.
Visible dark corruption / spiral markings on part of the face.
Battle-worn, dirty, exhausted, lightly bloodied.
Same established clothing.
Same established longer sword.
Exactly ONE sword only.
He holds the sword in ONE hand throughout the entire shot.
No weapon duplication.
No weapon switching.
No glowing eyes.

HOLLOW CHEST HARD LOCK:
The hero has a true open hollow chest cavity that is clearly see-through from both front and back.
Front opening to real empty space to rear opening.
The environment must be visible through the hollow whenever the angle allows.
Do not fill it in.
Do not place it in the stomach.
Do not cover the rear opening with intact clothing.
Do not have any hands, smoke, or limbs emerge from the hollow.

SHADOW HAND HARD LOCK:
All black arms and hands must emerge from cracks in the physical ground behind and beside the hero.
They are external manifestations of the realm.
They do not emerge from his body, clothing, chest, shoulders, or back.
The viewer must clearly understand:
cracked earth → black arm rises upward → hand reaches hero → hand grabs hero.
Most of the arms should come from behind him and pull backward from his shoulders, upper arms, upper back, and sides.

ENVIRONMENT:
The Anger Realm is massive, stormy, and hostile.
Dark fractured earth.
Steep damaged uphill path.
Ash, dust, and glowing ember particles constantly moving through the air.
Hurricane-force wind.
Hair and clothing whipping hard in the wind.
Huge rotating volumetric storm clouds overhead.
Lightning flashing in the distance.
Warped ruins and broken terrain in the far background.
Everything should feel alive, unstable, and epic.

0.00–1.80
Begin with a moving rear 3/4 medium-wide shot.
The older hero is already walking uphill against the wind, sword held low in one hand.
Cracks open in the ground behind and beside him.
From those cracks, multiple thin black arms rise visibly upward from the earth.
Show their forearms and elbows clearly before the hands make contact.
Several hands reach and latch onto his shoulders and upper arms.
The audience must clearly see that the arms come from the ground.

CAMERA:
Track with him from behind and slightly to the side, creating strong parallax between hero, grounded arms, drifting ash, and stormy background.

1.80–3.90
Cut to a side profile / side 3/4 tracking angle.
Several black arms remain visibly rooted in the terrain behind him and stretched toward his body.
They pull backward.
His body jerks slightly from the force.
He leans forward hard and plants his steps with effort.
His sword remains in one hand.
With his free arm or shoulder movement, he tries to shake off or peel away one grasp, but he never stops advancing.
His face shows physical strain, exhaustion, and determination.

3.90–5.60
Cut to a tight front / front 3/4 cinematic close-up.
Wind lashes his longer hair across his face.
We clearly see the facial corruption and the fatigue in his expression.
Behind his shoulders, black hands remain gripping him.
If the chest is visible, it must read clearly as a fully open, see-through hollow from front to back.
Lightning flashes in the background.
He looks close to his limit, but absolutely refuses to give up.

5.60–7.10
Cut wider.
Show the full spatial logic again.
The hero is still moving uphill in the foreground while multiple black arms remain physically connected to separate cracks in the ground several feet behind him.
Those arms are stretched tight from the strain as he keeps dragging himself forward.
He takes another difficult step, then another.
Some hands begin to slip.

7.10–8.00
Final payoff.
The hero drives forward with one last powerful burst of effort.
Several black hands lose their grip and slip from his shoulders and arms.
Their attached arms recoil backward toward the ground cracks they came from.
One last hand briefly trails across the back of his shoulder, then loses contact.

Strong cinematic motion throughout.
Tracking shots.
Subtle orbiting.
Foreground ash and ember occlusion.
Natural handheld weight without shakiness.
Strong depth and parallax.
No static camera.
No stiff posing.

Create a hyper-realistic studio portrait of an unforgettable male protagonist with a tan / olive-tan skin tone, designed to feel like a specific iconic lead, not a generic handsome fantasy model.
Core look:
adult male, around late 20s to late 30s
tan / olive-tan skin
medium-long dark hair, never short and never extra long, roughly ear-length to neck-length, with natural volume and texture
hair should have a few loose strands falling across the forehead and/or one side of the face
silver / steel / pale gray human eyes, not glowing, not supernatural
very minimal facial hair only: light stubble or faint scruff, never a heavy beard
strong masculine presence, haunted, intense, memorable, cinematic
Very important identity rule:
Make him feel like a real protagonist with a unique face, not just “a cool rugged guy.”
The underlying face must vary from image to image while staying attractive, believable, and memorable.
Randomize / vary these traits each time:
slightly different face shape
subtle facial asymmetry
different nose shapes: slightly crooked, broken, straighter, longer, wider, sharper, or more Roman
different brow shapes and brow asymmetry
different mouth shapes and lip structure
different jawlines and cheekbones
one eye slightly more hooded, heavier, or smaller than the other
mild under-eye wear, realistic skin texture, pores, faint blemishes, natural irregularities
slightly different hair styling each time while staying medium-long and dark
Scar rule:
Give him one memorable, realistic healed scar or scar pattern, but randomize the scar placement and shape each generation.
The scar should feel brutal, believable, old, and integrated into the face, not decorative.
Possible placement can vary between:
through eyebrow toward temple
across cheekbone
across the nose bridge
from cheek toward mouth line
short vertical forehead scar
broken scar near the eye
irregular scar near jawline
Keep it realistic, healed, and anatomically believable.
Mood / expression:
intense, brooding, soulful, slightly dangerous
calm but powerful
not smiling
emotionally complex, like a lead character with history
should feel memorable even without costume or environment
Framing / presentation:
tight head-and-shoulders portrait
plain neutral gray studio background
soft cinematic lighting
face-first composition
sharp detail on skin, hair, eyes, and scar
highly photoreal
rugged, dramatic, and premium-looking
Important “avoid” rules:
do not make him generic
do not make him look like a fashion model
do not give him short hair
do not give him extra-long hair
do not give him a thick beard
do not make the eyes glow
do not over-design the scar
do not over-stylize the background
do not make him too polished or too pretty
do not make all outputs look like the same exact man unless naturally emerging from the design
Overall goal:
Generate a distinctive, unforgettable, photoreal protagonist portrait with tan skin, medium-long dark hair, pale silver-gray eyes, minimal stubble, slight facial asymmetry, and a realistic memorable scar, while randomizing the underlying identity each time so every result feels like a different strong contender for the same hero concept.

Everything should reinforce the idea that this place consumes those who sit too long with regret.

- expression must feel sad, depressed, hollow, defeated
- black tears streaked down the face
- skin and hollow chest must be calcified, dry, pale, ashen, dead, paper-stone
- absolutely no pink fleshy skin
- armor and outfit must NOT be calcified, so they can be salvaged
- sword must be easily retrievable
- sword must NOT be held with two hands
- lower body must visibly be melting into the world
- tragic, beautiful, eerie, masterful tone

Medium-wide or cinematic discovery shot, clearly showing the failed predecessor, the retrievable sword, the salvageable armor, and the lower body melting into the Archive floor.

EXPENSIVE.

THE HERO FINDS A HUMAN-SIZED ROUTE INTO A DIFFERENT LOWER ARCHIVE DISTRICT.

IMAGE 6:

────────────────────────────────
HERO — ABSOLUTE LOCK
────────────────────────────────

Exact supplied hero.

Same face.
Same dark hair.
Same body proportions.
Same Library-era weathered clothing.
Same damage state.

ONE.

Not two.

Never duplicate the weapon.

No second sword on his back.
No sword appearing on his belt.
No second blade appearing in another hand.
No mirrored duplicate.
No floating duplicate.

The ONE exact supplied sword remains in the SAME HAND throughout the chase.

Long narrow corroded blade.
Elongated open negative-space center.
Dark twisted strands inside the opening.
Chipped edges.
Minimal guard.
Worn grip.
Tattered pommel strips.

NO generic longsword.
NO broad fantasy sword.
NO clean silver blade.
NO short sword.

HOLLOW HEART — EXTREME HARD LOCK
────────────────────────────────

THE HERO HAS A LARGE IRREGULAR TRUE HOLE THROUGH HIS THORACIC CHEST. <<<image_10>>>

THE HOLE PASSES COMPLETELY THROUGH HIS BODY.

FRONT TO BACK.

The rear of his torso is ALSO MISSING at the corresponding location.

The opening physically passes:

through the front chest,
through the sternum / ribcage,
and OUT THROUGH THE BACK.

REAL THREE-DIMENSIONAL NEGATIVE SPACE.

books,
shelves,
floating pages,
lights,
dust,
architecture

THROUGH HIS BODY.

THE SAME OPEN HOLE MUST REMAIN VISIBLE THROUGH HIS BACK.

His BACK CLOTHING is also torn away around the exit side of the Hollow.

No black patch.

No dark circular texture.

No membrane.

No fake shadow filling the center.

No partially healed torso.

No stomach hole.

The Hollow is centered through the THORAX / CHEST.

────────────────────────────────
HERO PERFORMANCE — CRITICAL
────────────────────────────────

The hero is RUNNING FOR HIS LIFE.

Do not make him look emotionally detached.

Do not make him look mildly concerned.

He is genuinely scared.

But he is still thinking.

His performance progresses:

RAW FEAR →
REALIZATION THE SPIDER IS GAINING →
FRANTIC SEARCH FOR A WAY OUT →
DESPERATE DECISION →
FULL COMMITMENT →
SHOCK WHEN THE ESCAPE WORKS →
IMMEDIATE CONTINUED FLIGHT.

FACIAL DETAIL:

eyes wide and highly alert,
rapid threat checks,
brows compressed,
jaw tense,
mouth slightly open from hard breathing,
nostrils flaring,
forehead strained,
fear visible around the eyes.

When he looks over his shoulder:

it should be a SHORT terrified glance.

Not a casual look.

His face should communicate:

“IT IS RIGHT BEHIND ME.”

His running is near maximum sustainable speed.

Forward body lean.
Hard arm drive.
Uneven exhausted stride.
Occasional traction correction on loose pages.
Heavy breathing affects shoulders and neck.

He never casually jogs.

PAPER-SPIDER — ABSOLUTE LOCK
────────────────────────────────

Use exact supplied paper-spider.

It is NOT a normal biological spider.

It is a grotesque LIVING BOOK / PAPER PREDATOR assembled from:

torn parchment,
folded pages,
old leather,
binding fibers,
splintered book structures,
ragged printed layers,
sharp page-like limbs,
distorted facial material.

It must move FAR MORE AGGRESSIVELY than previous generations.

NO stiff walking cycle.

It moves with violent intention:

explosive acceleration,
rapid multi-leg impacts,
sudden lateral corrections,
body compresses before lunging,
forelimbs stab around obstacles,
legs strike walls,
body climbs over debris without slowing,
shelves get smashed aside,
book carts overturn,
stacks collapse,
paper explodes through air,
architecture shakes from impacts.

The creature feels HEAVY even though it is partly paper.

Its FACE MUST CONSTANTLY LIVE AND REACT.

Eyes track hero.

Facial folds tighten.

Mouth changes shape.

Page-like teeth expose.

Printed / flesh-like facial structures twitch.

Expression progression:

PREDATORY FOCUS →
HUNGER →
ANGER →
EXTREME FRUSTRATION →
FURIOUS RAGE WHEN IT CANNOT FOLLOW.

No comedy.

It looks hateful and predatory.

NO-CONTACT RULE

NO CLAW CONTACT.

NO BODY COLLISION.

NO FACE TOUCHING HIS BACK.

NO LIMB CLIPPING THROUGH HIM.

Near misses must hit THE ENVIRONMENT instead.

A limb misses hero and destroys:
a shelf,
a railing,
a stack of books,
stone,
or wooden structure.

The danger comes from NEAR MISSES.

Not from glitched contact.

LIBRARY WORLD
────────────────────────────────

Colossal Depression Realm living archive.

Towering shelf canyons.
Cold cyan / sickly green atmospheric light.
Blackened timber.
Old stone.
Aged leather.
Parchment.
Suspended book bridges.
Impossible stacked-book architecture.
Floating pages at multiple depths.
Broken shelf structures.
Dust.
Loose bindings.
Huge shadowy voids between archive levels.

The Library feels endless and psychologically oppressive.

No generic castle.

No normal modern library.

ESCAPE MECHANISM — ABSOLUTE
────────────────────────────────

DO NOT end underneath the spider.

DO NOT put hero inside a dead-end hole.

DO NOT make him hide beside the monster.

The hero discovers a PHYSICAL ROUTE INTO A COMPLETELY DIFFERENT LOWER ARCHIVE DISTRICT.

Ahead:

a major suspended book walkway has collapsed.

A gigantic heavily loaded bookshelf has fallen diagonally from the upper level into a lower archive.

It forms a STEEP DESCENDING RAMP.

At the bottom:

a very narrow old masonry / shelf-service doorway.

Human shoulder-width.

Low ceiling.

Just large enough for the hero.

Beyond that opening is CLEARLY ANOTHER SPACE:

a long lower archive corridor,
deeper shelves,
different elevation,
multiple bends,
stair descent,
dark passages continuing far away.

It is not a closet.

It is not a crawlspace.

It is a ROUTE.

The paper-spider's broad central body is physically incapable of fitting through the doorway.

It may thrust forelimbs partially inside.

It cannot continue.

────────────────────────────────
SPEED-RAMP RULE
────────────────────────────────

Use ONLY TWO SHORT MOTIVATED SPEED RAMPS.

No constant speed ramping.

No music-video effect.

SPEED RAMP #1:
During one near-miss attack around 0:06.

Brief acceleration into the spider’s strike,
tiny fractional slowdown at the exact near-miss,
immediate snap back to real-time as hero escapes the hit.

SPEED RAMP #2:
When hero commits onto the collapsed shelf chute around 0:10.

Quick acceleration as he jumps onto it,
very brief controlled slowdown while his feet catch the unstable books,
then rapid real-time descent.

Both speed ramps should feel like premium action cinematography.

No cheesy slow motion.

────────────────────────────────
AUDIO — ABSOLUTE HARD LOCK
────────────────────────────────

NO MUSIC.

NO SCORE.

NO CINEMATIC STINGS.

NO HORROR STINGS.

NO TRAILER BOOMS.

NO BASS DROPS.

NO RISERS.

NO DRAMATIC WHOOSH ACCENTS.

NO SYNTHETIC IMPACT HITS.

NO CHOIR.

NO DIALOGUE.

THE HERO NEVER SPEAKS.

NO MOUTHING WORDS.

NO “OH SHIT.”

NO SELF-TALK.

NO FINAL LINE.

Mouth opens ONLY for:
hard breathing,
physical exertion,
brief involuntary breath.

DIEGETIC SOUND ONLY:

hero's boots,
labored breathing,
cloth,
one sword moving in his hand,
paper whipping,
books falling,
spider limbs striking stone,
wood breaking,
shelves collapsing,
binding fibers tearing,
debris,
creature’s nonverbal snarling / paper rage,
deep library structural creaks.

────────────────────────────────
0:00–0:02.0 — FULL PANIC
────────────────────────────────

START ALREADY AT FULL SPEED.

NO INTRODUCTION.

28mm low side-rear tracking.

Hero sprints violently through the Library.

He is visibly terrified.

Camera is only several feet away.

His face is readable in profile.

He makes a quick frightened look behind him—

eyes widen—

SPIDER IS CLOSER THAN EXPECTED.

His reaction is immediate.

He pushes harder.

One sword locked in his hand.

Pages whip across lens.

Foreground shelving produces intense parallax.

Through one side angle:

the TRUE Hollow passes completely through hero's chest and back.

Moving cyan-lit shelving is clearly visible THROUGH his body.

────────────────────────────────
0:02.0–0:04.0 — THE SPIDER DESTROYS THE PATH
────────────────────────────────

Hard motivated cut behind a foreground shelf edge.

24mm aggressive monster tracking.

Spider violently pursues.

NO stiff stepping.

It barrels through the archive.

One forelimb knocks an entire book cart sideways.

Another limb smashes through stacked volumes.

A hanging shelf collapses behind it.

Paper erupts everywhere.

Its face continuously tracks hero.

Eyes narrow.

Mouth tightens.

Its expression becomes furious.

Keep this shot SHORT.

Return immediately to hero.

────────────────────────────────
0:04.0–0:06.4 — OBSTACLE / NEAR DEATH
────────────────────────────────

35mm front three-quarter tracking while hero runs toward camera.

A collapsed shelf blocks most of pathway.

Hero rapidly scans:

left blocked.
right blocked.
center narrow.

He changes line without stopping.

He jumps / vaults the lowest section.

Not a flip.

Not acrobatic posing.

A desperate ugly survival movement.

As he lands—

the spider launches a long sharp forelimb toward the place he is moving through.

SPEED RAMP #1:

brief acceleration into attack.

Fractional slowdown:

hero sees it,
eyes flare,
torso twists sharply,
shoulder drops.

The limb passes several inches behind him.

NO CONTACT.

Immediately return to full speed.

The spider limb DESTROYS the railing instead.

Wood,
books,
paper,
dust explode outward.

Hero nearly loses footing.

One hand touches ground for half a step—

then he is RUNNING again.

────────────────────────────────
0:06.4–0:08.7 — HE SEES THE ONLY WAY OUT
────────────────────────────────

Camera changes to a slightly elevated lateral angle.

Ahead and BELOW:

THE COLLAPSED BOOKSHELF CHUTE.

We already glimpse:

steep diagonal shelf,
unstable books,
lower archive,
tiny doorway at bottom.

Hero's eyes lock onto it.

His face says:

“That’s it.”

No words.

He looks behind once.

Spider has recovered and is charging again.

Hero immediately angles for chute.

────────────────────────────────
0:08.7–0:11.3 — COMMIT
────────────────────────────────

Hero reaches the broken edge.

No stopping.

He jumps onto the enormous tilted bookshelf.

SPEED RAMP #2:

quick acceleration into jump.

Brief controlled slowdown as both boots hit sliding books.

Pages and volumes collapse beneath his feet.

Then FULL SPEED.

He half-runs, half-slides downward.

Camera descends beside him at high speed.

Sword stays in ONE HAND,
pressed tight alongside his body.

His other hand briefly catches shelf structure to maintain balance.

His expression remains terrified and focused.

Above:

the spider aggressively launches onto the tilted structure after him.

Its weight causes shelf sections to BREAK.

────────────────────────────────
0:11.3–0:13.7 — DESCENDING CHAOS
────────────────────────────────

Rapid 2–3 shot sequence.

LOW SIDE:
hero skids downward between tumbling books.

REAR THREE-QUARTER:
clearly show his BACK.

CRITICAL:

The Hollow remains OPEN THROUGH HIS BACK.

There is no rear fabric closing it.

Light and falling pages are visibly seen through the back opening and out through the front.

FRONT CLOSE:
his eyes snap toward narrow doorway below.

He knows he has seconds.

Spider is destroying the shelf above him as it descends.

Not reaching him yet.

────────────────────────────────
0:13.7–0:15.4 — HUMAN-SIZED EXIT
────────────────────────────────

Hero reaches bottom.

The narrow doorway is directly ahead.

He does NOT stop.

He lowers head,
turns shoulder,
pulls his ONE sword flat alongside his body,

and SHOOTS THROUGH.

Camera leads him into opening.

As he rotates sideways—

environment is visibly seen through the FRONT-TO-BACK chest Hollow.

Hero clears doorway and immediately stumbles into the LOWER ARCHIVE.

He catches himself.

Keeps running.

────────────────────────────────
0:15.4–0:17.3 — CREATURE CANNOT FOLLOW
────────────────────────────────

Low reverse shot from lower archive looking back.

The spider comes down the chute at brutal speed.

It attempts to enter after him—

CRASH.

Its huge broad central body SLAMS into the narrow stone / shelf doorway.

Forelegs penetrate partially.

BODY CANNOT.

No clipping.

No magical squeezing.

The opening is visibly too small.

The creature violently tries to force itself through.

Stone cracks.

Paper fibers tear.

Its face presses toward the opening.

Its expression becomes PURE FURY.

Eyes fixed on hero.

Mouth / page-teeth flex.

Face shakes with rage.

It claws the floor.

It CANNOT FOLLOW.

────────────────────────────────
0:17.3–0:18.5 — HERO REALIZES
────────────────────────────────

85mm moving close-up.

Hero is STILL MOVING AWAY.

He turns his head backward only briefly.

Face:

terrified,
breathing violently,
disbelief.

His eyes confirm:

THE SPIDER IS STUCK.

No smile.

No smugness.

No dialogue.

One hard breath.

He turns forward immediately.

────────────────────────────────
0:18.5–0:20.0 — HE ACTUALLY GETS AWAY
────────────────────────────────

Camera retreats ahead of hero.

He runs rapidly into a visibly different LOWER ARCHIVE DISTRICT.

The space opens into:

lower towering shelves,
a descending stone stair,
multiple dark routes,
hanging pages,
deep green-cyan atmosphere.

He runs down the first turn.

Architecture moves BETWEEN HIM AND THE SPIDER.

Through the shrinking distant doorway behind:

the spider is still violently struggling but unable to enter.

Hero makes another turn.

NOW THE SPIDER CAN NO LONGER SEE HIM.

He disappears deeper into the lower archive.

END WHILE HERO IS STILL RUNNING.

CUT.

────────────────────────────────
CAMERA MASTER LOCK
────────────────────────────────

Every shot must have a purpose.

No shot longer than approximately 2.5 seconds unless necessary for the chute action.

Camera sequence:

low sprint tracking,
violent spider insert,
front hero obstacle coverage,
speed-ramped near miss,
elevated escape reveal,
descending side camera,
rear three-quarter Hollow proof,
tight doorway passage,
reverse creature impact,
hero reaction macro,
moving lower-archive escape.

Use natural visual wipes:

pages,
shelf edges,
falling books,
columns,
foreground bindings.

No fades.

No random orbiting.

No spinning camera.

No generic drone shot.

No static final frame.

────────────────────────────────
ANTI-COMEDY LOCK
────────────────────────────────

Everything is treated seriously.

No exaggerated funny stumbling.

No cartoon monster bouncing.

No silly facial expressions.

No playful chase rhythm.

No monster conveniently waiting.

No superhero acrobatics.

Hero movements are imperfect because he is exhausted,
but they remain physically believable and desperate.

The spider should feel like a creature from a nightmare,
not an amusement-park chase.

────────────────────────────────
FAIL CONDITIONS
────────────────────────────────

FAIL if hero has two swords.

FAIL if hero loses sword.

FAIL if sword changes.

FAIL if front Hollow closes.

FAIL if back Hollow closes.

FAIL if rear clothing covers the Hollow.

FAIL if the cavity becomes black or filled.

FAIL if spider bites hero.

FAIL if spider touches hero.

FAIL if hero looks nonchalant.

FAIL if hero casually jogs.

FAIL if hero talks.

FAIL if hero mouths words.

FAIL if music appears.

FAIL if trailer stings appear.

FAIL if spider moves stiffly.

FAIL if spider face stays frozen.

FAIL if hero ends trapped beneath spider.

FAIL if hero stops after doorway.

FAIL if destination is a dead end.

FAIL if spider follows through the narrow exit.

FINAL STORY READ:

HE IS TERRIFIED.

THE CREATURE IS GAINING.

HE SEES ONE IMPOSSIBLE HUMAN-SIZED ROUTE.

HE COMMITS.

THE SPIDER'S SIZE BECOMES ITS FAILURE.

IT GETS BLOCKED.

HE DOES NOT CELEBRATE.

HE RUNS UNTIL IT CANNOT SEE HIM ANYMORE.

TEMPORARY ESCAPE.

NO COMEDY.

NO GLITCHED CONTACT.

NO SECOND SWORD.

TRUE FRONT-TO-BACK HOLLOW AT ALL TIMES.

prompt:
20 SECONDS — 16:9 WIDESCREEN

8K IMAX. Photorealistic live-action — no 3D-render look, no game-engine look, no game-cutscene aesthetic, no visible CGI aesthetic. Premium invisible VFX only. Hyper-real feature-film realism, extremely tactile materials, realistic atmospheric depth, subtle film grain, expensive lensing, emotionally devastating acting, no painterly finish, no stiff staging.

Create a 20-second cinematic emotional breakdown sequence in the Anger Realm. This is a SOLO hero scene. No boss. No enemies visible. No dialogue. No voiceover. No music. Diegetic sound only: ragged breathing, ash blowing across stone, faint ember crackle, distant low environmental groans, subtle memory-sound intrusions such as receding footsteps, a door closing, faint fabric rustle, and brief fragmented childlike ambience.

The hero is the final aged version: slightly longer dirty hair hanging partly into his face, light beard, more scars, battle damage, ash and grime on skin and armor, some dried blood around the mouth, and the Hollow Heart cavity in his chest must remain visibly open and fully see-through whenever the torso is shown. This is critical. The chest hole must not fill in, flatten, or become visually blocked. Preserve the exact design.

ANGER REALM color lock: scorched black, charcoal, soot-gray, dark cinder brown, burnt umber, smoke haze, weathered dark iron, bone-dust gray, restrained ember-red and dim furnace orange in cracks and drifting sparks. No pink or magenta atmosphere. Keep the realm oppressive, dry, and heat-scorched.

The environment must feel massive and hyper-real, not painterly. Surround him with monumental fractured humanoid structures in the distance: colossal leaning bodies fused into the terrain, broken enraged faces, cracked torsos, twisted trees with spiraling branch systems, floating fragmented pieces hanging in the smoky air, layered ash haze, drifting embers, and subtle heat distortion. The hero must look tiny against this environment.

Important camera rule: the camera should never feel static. Every shot should have motivated motion — slow creeping push-ins, low-angle drifting, subtle handheld instability during the breakdown, small parallax moves, restrained cinematic arcs. No locked-off dead shots.

0:00–0:03 — Begin immediately with the hero already emotionally unstable. Very low-angle wide shot near the ground, lens around 24mm, slowly creeping forward. The hero is small in frame, isolated in the enormous Anger Realm. Giant broken enraged humanoid structures tower behind him. He is breathing hard, disoriented, dirty, bloodied, ash-covered. His sword is either hanging loosely or already lowered near him. He looks around as if realizing he is completely alone.

0:03–0:06 — Cut to a moving medium close-up, 50mm to 85mm, slowly drifting around him. He tries to steady his breathing but fails. His eyes water rapidly. His face tightens, jaw trembles, and he is fighting to keep control. He shakes his head slightly as if rejecting what he is feeling. He glances off into empty space, listening for something that is not there.

0:06–0:08 — First memory intrusion, brief and clear. Show symbolic abandonment imagery, not random surrealism: a small child silhouette standing alone in an open field while distant figures walk away; then a warm-lit doorway slowly left empty; then a hand slipping out of another hand. These flashes should feel like fragmented memory shards, very brief, emotionally readable, and traumatic because of absence. Then cut back to the hero.

0:08–0:11 — Low three-quarter shot with camera slowly circling. His composure fully starts collapsing. His sword slips from his hand and drops hard to the ground. He drops to one knee, then nearly both, catching himself with one hand. His shoulders begin shaking. He is not posing heroically — he is unraveling. Show the chest hole clearly in at least one angle here, visibly open and see-through.

0:11–0:14 — Intimate close-up, slight handheld instability. Tears now pour down through dirt and blood. He tries to hold back sobs, pressing a shaking hand partly over his mouth or lower face. His breathing stutters and fails. His expression should feel humiliated, frightened, overwhelmed, and deeply human. He is trying not to fall apart and failing.

0:14–0:16 — Stronger memory intrusion montage. Keep it simple and emotionally universal: an empty chair at a table, a child’s object left behind in a quiet room, distant backs turning away, a hallway with no one coming back, warm light disappearing from a doorway. The core idea must read clearly: he has spent his life being left behind. These flashes should hit harder and faster.

0:16–0:18 — Return to the hero in a dramatic low-angle wide shot. He is tiny in the foreground on one knee or almost folded over, sobbing uncontrollably while the colossal Anger Realm looms over him. The camera creeps laterally for subtle parallax. Ash and ember particles drift through foreground. The environment must feel massive, photoreal, oppressive, and legendary. This should be one of the most iconic shots in the film.

0:18–0:20 — Final emotional close-up. Camera pushes in slowly. He lifts his face slightly, tears everywhere, breathing broken, eyes looking toward nothing. A final brief memory impression hits him — not literal exposition, just the feeling of being abandoned again. His face collapses completely and he bows inward, sobbing hard. End on raw vulnerability, not recovery.

Performance hard lock: this is not elegant crying. This is a brutal emotional collapse. He should look like a man who has carried abandonment trauma for years and can no longer contain it. Wet eyes, full tears, trembling jaw, shaking shoulders, unstable breathing, involuntary sobbing, moments of trying to suppress it and failing. Make it raw, masculine, painful, and deeply human.

Do not make him scream theatrically at the sky. Do not make it melodramatic fantasy posing. Do not beautify the grief. Make it intimate, devastating, and real.

- Hero must remain small in wide shots
- Camera must always be subtly moving
- Hollow Heart cavity must remain visibly open and see-through when shown
- Environment must be more photoreal and dimensional, less painterly
- Memory flashes must clearly communicate abandonment / being left alone
- The entire scene must feel expensive, cinematic, and emotionally unforgettable

prompt:

NO GENERATED VOICEOVER.
NO MUSIC.
NO SCORE.
NO CHOIR.
NO CHANTING.

Production sound only:
living hero's breathing,
boots on broken wood and stone,
ancient shelf creaks,
paper drifting,
cloth and leather movement,
tiny calcified fragments falling,
dry mineral cracking,
metal grinding against a petrified grip,
distant Library room tone.

REF 1 is ABSOLUTE CANON for the DEAD BODY.
Preserve the corpse's exact:
pose,
identity,
armor,
calcification,
bookshelf integration,
left-shoulder stab wound,
fully open Hollow chest cavity, <<<image_3>>>
dead facial expression,
and sword placement.

REF 2 and REF 3 control the LIVING HERO.

REF 4 controls BOTH Hollow cavities. <<<image_3>>>

CRITICAL STORY RULE:

There are exactly TWO versions of the same man in this scene:

1. THE LIVING HERO.
2. HIS PREVIOUS DEAD BODY.

The corpse is completely, permanently DEAD.

It NEVER:
breathes,
blinks,
moves its eyes,
moves its head,
moves its chest,
moves voluntarily,
reacts,
awakens,
speaks,
or comes back to life.

The corpse moves ONLY passively if the living hero physically pushes or pulls against its calcified hand/wrist.

The living hero begins the scene EMPTY-HANDED.

There is exactly ONE sword.

The sword begins locked in the dead body's hand.

the book faces on the books must be moving 

────────────────────────────
0:00–0:02 — SOMETHING FAMILIAR
────────────────────────────

Start immediately with an extremely low 24mm tracking shot moving backward through the Cursed Library.

Foreground books and broken shelf fragments whip past close to lens.

The living hero walks slowly into frame.

He is dirty, lightly bloodied, exhausted from resurrection, slightly armored, with early black corruption visible on part of one hand.

NO sword in either hand.

The camera stays below waist height.

Ahead of him, partially obscured by shelves, we glimpse the metallic edge of a familiar blade.

He slows instantly.

His breathing becomes quieter.

Do NOT reveal the corpse yet.

────────────────────────────
0:02–0:04 — THE BLADE
────────────────────────────

MACRO 85–100mm.

Begin on the sword blade resting naturally across rubble and the dead body's legs.

Camera performs a controlled creeping travel ALONG THE BLADE:

blade →
guard →
grip →

until we discover—

A CALCIFIED HUMAN HAND locked around the hilt.

The fingers are stone-gray, cracked and completely rigid.

Tiny ash particles fall from one knuckle.

Then camera continues upward just enough to reveal the open Hollow chest.

The audience begins realizing who this is.

────────────────────────────
0:04–0:06.3 — REVEAL HIM
────────────────────────────

Cut wider through a foreground bookshelf occlusion.

Reveal the entire calcified previous hero exactly like REF 1.

Same face.
Same armor.
Same Hollow.
Same left-shoulder stab wound.
Same sword.
Same body fused into the Library.

His upper chest  contains the deep old sword wound:
torn armor,
calcified damaged flesh,
dark dried blood remnants,
mineralized trauma.

He looks completely lifeless and partially swallowed by books, blackened wood, paper fibers and mineral growth.

Hold only long enough for recognition.

────────────────────────────
0:06.3–0:08 — LIVING HERO REACTION
────────────────────────────

CUT HARD to an intimate 85mm close-up of the living hero.

Superb restrained acting.

His eyes immediately recognize his own face.

His breath catches.

A tiny involuntary recoil.

His jaw tightens.

He looks at:

the dead face →
the left-shoulder wound →
the Hollow →
the sword.

His eyes become slightly wet.

He makes one very small head shake.

No screaming.
No melodrama.
No spoken "no."

It should look like a real human being confronting his own corpse.

────────────────────────────
0:08–0:10 — HE HAS TO TOUCH IT
────────────────────────────

Over-the-shoulder 35mm push as he approaches.

Camera stays close enough that his living shoulder partially obscures frame.

He crouches beside the corpse.

For one uncomfortable second he looks directly into his own dead face from less than two feet away.

Then his eyes move down toward the sword.

His dirty, partially black-corrupted hand slowly reaches toward the hilt.

It stops approximately one inch away.

His fingers hesitate.

His breathing is audible.

Then he forces himself to touch it.

0:10–0:12 — LIVING HAND / DEAD HAND
────────────────────────────

100mm extreme macro.

The living hero's partially black-corrupted hand closes around the sword grip immediately above the corpse's calcified fingers.

LIVING BLACKENED FINGERS
touching
DEAD CALCIFIED FINGERS
on the SAME weapon.

Hold briefly.

Hero pulls.

Nothing happens.

Hero looks disturbed.

He pulls again slightly harder.

Still locked.

────────────────────────────

Fast intimate cuts.

Hero braces the corpse's calcified wrist with his free hand.

his thumb presses beneath one petrified finger.

SHOT C:
close profile on hero's face, disgust / grief / determination mixing together.

SHOT D — macro:
he physically PRIES the dead index finger away from the grip.

CRACK.

The finger joint fractures like brittle mineralized tissue the fingers should break off.

Tiny gray fragments fall onto the sword guard.

Hero flinches subtly at the sound.

He has just broken his own dead finger.

No gore explosion.
No severed hand.
Just horrifying tactile calcification.

────────────────────────────

────────────────────────────

Hero commits.

He braces harder.

Several calcified fingers fracture incrementally around the grip:

CRACK.
CRACK.

Small ash-mineral fragments fall.

Metal SCRAPES loudly through the petrified hand.

With one final controlled pull—

THE SWORD BREAKS FREE.

The sudden release shifts the living hero backward slightly.

Real weight.
Real momentum.

He catches himself.

The corpse remains COMPLETELY motionless.

One calcified finger remains frozen half-open where the sword used to be.

────────────────────────────
0:16.5–0:17.8 — WHAT WAS LEFT BEHIND
────────────────────────────

Extreme close insert.

Living hero looks down at the weapon.

His black-corrupted fingers tighten around the hilt.

Rack focus past the sword to his previous dead hand in the background—

now empty.

Then rack focus farther to the calcified dead face.

No movement.

No blinking.

Dead.

The hero realizes this body truly stayed here.

0:17.8–0:19 — WALK AWAY
────────────────────────────

────────────────────────────
0:19–0:20 — ONE LAST LOOK
────────────────────────────

As he walks away—

he stops for only half a beat.

Without fully turning his body, he looks back over one shoulder.

Camera cuts to his face for an extremely brief intimate look:

fear,
grief,
acceptance,
and the understanding that this place can keep taking versions of him.

Then he faces forward again.

He keeps walking.

Sword low at his side.

The calcified corpse becomes smaller behind him.

CUT TO ABSOLUTE BLACK.

END TRAILER.

────────────────────────────
CORPSE ABSOLUTE LOCK
────────────────────────────

The previous body is DEAD for the entire 20 seconds.

ZERO:
breathing,
blinking,
eye movement,
facial movement,
head movement,
mouth movement,
chest motion,
finger movement by itself.

Even when the sword is pulled, only the PHYSICALLY CONTACTED calcified fingers crack because the living hero is forcing them apart.

The rest of the corpse stays completely inert.

It is architecture now.

────────────────────────────
SWORD CONTINUITY LOCK
────────────────────────────

Exactly ONE sword exists.

At 0:00 the living hero is EMPTY-HANDED.

Sword belongs to the corpse.

Living hero must physically:

DISCOVER →
APPROACH →
TOUCH →
PULL →
FAIL →
BRACE →
PRY OPEN THE DEAD FINGERS →
BREAK CALCIFIED GRIP →
FREE THE SWORD →
WALK AWAY WITH IT.

books,
wood,
smoke,
flesh,
armor,
shadow material.

wet eyes,
